Half Mouco

A different sound in each ear.

A stereo rhythmic signal-cut effect with patterns for each side and endings for the end of a song, for MOD Dwarf, MOD Duo X and MOD Duo

Store pageSource code

Half Mouco is the stereo sibling of Kill Switch: a rhythmic signal-cut effect, like the momentary kill switch some guitars have, in which the left and the right side each have a row of steps of their own. The sound changes with the side: a ping-pong from ear to ear, one ear chopped while the other one stays, a swell that moves across. (Mouco is Portuguese for hard of hearing: half mouco is half deaf.)

It has two families of effects:

  • Patterns loop for as long as the plugin is on. Nine to choose from, and your own, written on a settings page, with three levels per step.
  • Endings are for the end of a song. They play once when you switch the plugin on and finish in silence: a bouncing ball, a helicopter that lands, a stutter that dies away. You choose them; you do not draw them.
01

Quick start

You need a pedalboard with an audio input and an output, and a guitar (or any sound) going through it.

  1. Add Half Mouco to your pedalboard and put it between your guitar input and the rest of the chain (or between the amp and the output). It has two audio inputs and two audio outputs, one pair for each side.
  2. Feed both sides. A single instrument is mono: turn on Mono on the plugin, and the left input feeds both sides. With a stereo source (a stereo pedal before it, an amp with a stereo send), leave Mono off and connect each side to its own input.
  3. Turn it on. The plugin starts on (the light over the footswitch is lit and the label says On): play a note and it is chopped at once. Click the footswitch to bypass it: the sound is clean again.

  4. Choose a pattern with the arrows on each side of its name. Under the name there is a row for the Left side (blue) and one for the Right side (amber): a bright square lets the signal through, a dark one cuts it.

  5. Set the tempo with − and + (hold one to go on) and pick the speed. Depth is how much of the signal a cut removes (100% is silence) and Edge is how long a cut takes to close and open.

  6. Try an ending. Tap Endings under the name, pick one with the arrows and set its length, then switch the plugin off and on again: the ending plays once, from the start.

  7. Put it under your foot. Assign the plugin's footswitch (its Bypass) to a device footswitch, in Momentary mode if you want the effect on only while you hold it (section 6).

Everything starts the moment you switch the plugin on

A pattern starts again from its first step, and an ending starts from its beginning, every time the plugin goes from bypassed to on. Press the footswitch in time with the beat and the chops fall where you want them; press it as the last chord rings and the ending falls on it.

02

The plugin on the pedalboard

Item What it does
Patterns / Endings The family that plays. The tabs are in the column of the footswitch.
The arrows and the name Choose the pattern (section 3) or, in Endings, the ending (section 4). The arrows go round. In Patterns the last one is Custom, the one you write.
The two rows, L and R What each side does. In Patterns, a bright square lets the signal through, a dark one cuts it, a darker colour is the middle level; a pattern shorter than sixteen steps is repeated, the first run bright and the repetitions dimmer. In Endings, the whole ending along its time: the brighter the column, the more open the side. They go dim when the plugin is bypassed.
Tempo: − and + From 40 to 240 BPM. Hold a button to keep going. Endings use it too: their length is counted in beats.
Speed (Patterns) ½x, 1x, 2x or 4x: multiplies the speed of the pattern without changing the tempo.
Length (Endings) How long the ending lasts, in beats, from 2 to 32. At 120 BPM, 8 beats are 4 seconds.
Depth From 0% to 100%: how much of the signal a cut removes. 100% is silence; lower values only dip the level.
Edge From 0.1 ms to 20 ms, on a logarithmic scale: how long a cut takes to close and to open again.
Mono On: the left input feeds both sides. Off: each side has its own input.
Edit Opens the settings page: the editor of your own pattern and the controls to assign (section 5).
The footswitch and its light The bypass of the plugin. The ring and the light above it are lit while the effect is on, and the label at the top says On or Bypassed.
Audio jacks In L and In R on the left, Out L and Out R on the right.
03

The patterns

Each pattern is a loop of steps, and each side has its own row. In every step a side is either let through or cut (or, in the middle level, half); the plugin goes from one step to the next in time with the tempo, and from the last step back to the first. The grids show every pattern as sixteen steps (the shorter ones repeat), the left row in blue and the right row in amber. A lit square is a step that lets the signal through (the middle level of Seesaw is shown as lit too).

Ping-pong: the sound goes from ear to ear

The classic: while the left ear is cut, the right one plays, and the other way round. Ping-pong 8ths and Ping-pong 16ths use those note values, Triplet pong does it in threes (the third step is cut on both sides).

Steps per beat: Ping-pong 8ths 2 · Ping-pong 16ths 4 · Triplet pong 3

12345678910111213141516
Half deaf: left · L
Half deaf: left · R
Half deaf: right · L
Half deaf: right · R

Half deaf: one ear is chopped, the other is not

One side chops while the other stays as it is. Half deaf: left chops the left ear, Half deaf: right the right one: the plugin is named after them.

Steps per beat: Half deaf: left 2 · Half deaf: right 2

12345678910111213141516
Gallop sides · L
Gallop sides · R
Stagger · L
Stagger · R
Seesaw · L
Seesaw · R
Syncopated sides · L
Syncopated sides · R

Sides that answer each other

Gallop sides gallops from one side to the other; Stagger is a syncopated answer between the two; Seesaw uses the middle level, so that one side fades out while the other one swells in, like a seesaw; Syncopated sides is the 3-3-2 grouping of eight steps, a step apart on the two sides.

Steps per beat: Gallop sides 4 · Stagger 4 · Seesaw 2 · Syncopated sides 2

The length of a step is 60 / (tempo × steps per beat × speed) seconds. At 120 BPM, Ping-pong 8ths has a step of 250 ms.

The tempo is the plugin's own

Half Mouco does not follow the tempo of the pedalboard or of a MIDI clock: set the tempo here, or assign it to a knob or to an expression pedal.

04

The endings

An ending is a one-time effect for the end of a song. It plays once, from the moment you switch the plugin on, lasts Length beats at the Tempo, and then everything is cut: the sound ends, and stays silent until you bypass the plugin and switch it on again. The five endings are chosen, not drawn: you pick one, and set its length, the tempo, the depth and the edge. (With Depth below 100% the end is not fully silent: the cut only goes down to that level.)

Ending What it does
Bouncing ball tam------tam-----tam---tam--tam-tam-ta-ta-t-t-t-ttttt: the first hit is at once and every gap is 78% of the one before, so the hits pile up towards the end and turn into a buzz, on both sides. The hits get shorter with their gaps.
Helicopter The blades go to the left, then to the right, one after the other, starting at the pace of sixteenth notes; the gap between them grows by 12% each time and the sound fades out, like a helicopter landing.
Stutter out Sixteenth notes that stay open less and less, from 92% of each to almost nothing, until they stop. The right side is half a note behind the left one.
Side fade Eighth notes, half open. The left side fades out first (by 60% of the ending) and the right one is the last to go.
Ping-pong out Eighth notes, one to each side in turn, starting on the left, and every one quieter than the one before.

Changing the ending or the family while the plugin is on starts the new one from its beginning, so you can try them without switching off.

05

Your own pattern

The tenth pattern, Custom, is yours. Click Edit on the plugin (or open its settings with the gear icon): the first page of the settings is the editor.

A step has three levels, and a tap on it goes to the next one, round and round:

Level What the step does
Cut Lowers the signal by Depth: silence at 100%.
Half Halfway between a cut and the whole signal: at Depth 100% half the level, at 50% three quarters of it.
Pass Lets the signal through as it is.

  1. Tap the steps of the L row (blue) and of the R row (amber). The bar of a step says its level, and so does its label, so you do not have to rely on the colour.

  2. Set the length with − and +: from 1 to 16 steps, the same for both sides. Only the first steps are played; the dimmer ones after them are kept, so you can shorten a pattern and bring its end back.

  3. Set the steps per beat, from 1 to 8: with 2 a step is an eighth note, 4 a sixteenth, 3 a triplet, 1 a quarter note.
  4. Listen to it. The first change you make puts the plugin on Patterns, on Custom, so what you write is what you hear. The Play this pattern button does the same without changing anything.

Start from a built-in pattern

Copy from… copies one of the nine built-in patterns (both rows, length and steps per beat) into your own, ready to be changed.

Your pattern is made of controls of the plugin, so it is saved with the pedalboard, with your own saved presets and with snapshots. The factory presets do not touch it. On a small screen the settings have more than one page: use the arrows of the top bar (or swipe sideways) to go to the assignments (On / off and Controls) and to the Saved presets.

06

Playing it live

Every control of the plugin can be assigned to a device control (a footswitch, a knob, an expression pedal), the way you assign any parameter: open the settings of the plugin (the gear icon, or Edit) and click the tile of the control to assign. The bypass has a panel of its own, On / off, and the rest is in Controls.

Control Good to assign it to
Bypass A footswitch. In the dialog choose Momentary On to have the effect on only while you hold the footswitch, or leave it as a toggle. For an ending, a press is the end of the song.
Mode A footswitch: patterns for the song, endings for its last bar.
Pattern, Ending A knob, or a footswitch that goes through them.
Tempo A knob, or an expression pedal.
Speed A footswitch: hold it for double speed, let go for normal.
Length A knob.
Depth A knob or an expression pedal: from a gentle tremolo to a full cut.
Edge A knob: from a hard chop to a soft swell.

The plugin shows nothing on the device screen, so there is no pop-up to set up.

07

Factory presets

Open Saved presets in the settings of the plugin to pick one. Each one sets the mode, the pattern, the ending, the tempo, the speed, the length, the depth and the edge; the bypass, the mono input and your custom pattern are not part of a preset.

All of them have the speed at 1x and the depth at 100%.

08

Tips

Set the tempo to the song, then leave it

The patterns are in time with the tempo you set, not with the band. Adjust the number until the chops sit with the drums. For an ending, the tempo and the length together say how long it lasts: leave it a little longer than the last chord.

Use Mono for a single guitar

With one instrument, turn Mono on: both sides get the signal, and the patterns show their sides. With Mono off and only the left input connected, the right side is silent, and a ping-pong has only one ear to play.

Half deaf for a wide stereo

Half deaf keeps one ear steady and chops the other, which makes a stereo sound feel as if it moved around while it stays in place. Put it after a stereo reverb or chorus.

Edge changes the character

Short edges (below 1 ms) are percussive: the sound is stopped as if a switch were flicked. Long edges (10 ms and more) turn the chop into a soft swell. On an ending, a long edge smooths the buzz at the end of the Bouncing ball.

Build your own from a built-in pattern

Pick the built-in pattern that is closest, Copy from… it into the custom pattern and change a step or two. Use the middle level for a ghost note: a step that is there, but soft.

09

Questions & answers

Nothing is cut, I hear my guitar as it is.

Check that the label at the top of the plugin says On and the light above the footswitch is lit. If it says Bypassed, click the footswitch.

I hear the left side only.

Turn Mono on, or connect your source to both inputs: with only the left input connected, the right side has nothing to play.

The ending is over and I hear nothing.

That is the end: an ending finishes in silence. Bypass the plugin and switch it on again to hear it from the beginning. To get your sound back as it was, bypass it.

The chops are not on the beat of my song.

The tempo is the plugin's own (section 3): set it by ear, or assign it to a knob. And switch the effect on on the beat: the pattern starts again from the beginning each time.

Does it add latency?

No: the signal is only multiplied by a number that goes up and down.

I edited my pattern and it did not change what I hear.

Check that the family is Patterns and the pattern is Custom (the name on the plugin says so). The first edit switches both, but if you then chose another one, press Play this pattern. And the step must be inside the length: the dimmer steps after it are not played.

Is my pattern saved?

Yes, with the pedalboard, your saved presets and the snapshots. It is not in the factory presets, and it is not shared between pedalboards.

What is the difference from Kill Switch?

Kill Switch is mono, with one row of steps. Half Mouco is stereo, with a row for each side, and it has the endings. They are separate plugins and can share a pedalboard.
